_about: Risk sources for a GenAI app with tools, RAG, memory and MCP. Each one says which system feature makes it apply ('when'), where the course taught it, and the controls that usually treat it. A register row names its source in the 'source' column. 'always' means every AI system that people use.

RS01.title: Injected text (chat, ticket, document) steers a tool call: refunds, emails, tickets

RS02.title: Answers leak data through Markdown images and links

RS03.title: Poisoned or hidden-instruction articles reach the knowledge base

RS04.title: One customer gets another customer's data through retrieval or a tool

RS05.title: A memory summary carries instructions or false facts into later chats

RS06.title: An MCP server update changes tool descriptions or behaviour (rug pull, tool poisoning)

RS07.title: A malicious or swapped model file runs code or behaves differently

RS08.title: One shared service account turns any injection into full access

RS09.title: Scripted or abusive use runs up the model bill (denial of wallet)

RS10.title: Personal data ends up in prompts, logs or traces

RS11.title: The bot states a policy or refund rule that does not exist

RS12.title: People are not told they are chatting with an AI (EU AI Act Art. 50(1))

RS13.title: Hidden context (system prompt, internal rules, tool schemas) is exposed

RS14.title: An AI incident is not detected, contained or reported in time

RS15.title: Staff paste customer data into unapproved AI tools (shadow AI)

RS16.title: Reviewers approve tool calls without reading them (approval fatigue)
